blocks.label: Definition
blocks.html: The Mann-Whitney U test (also called the Wilcoxon rank-sum test) compares two independent groups. It ranks all observations together and tests whether values in one group tend to be larger than values in the other. Its null hypothesis is that a randomly chosen value from group 1 is equally likely to be larger or smaller than a randomly chosen value from group 2.

blocks.label: Simplified Explanation
blocks.html: Pool both groups and rank every value from smallest (rank 1) to largest, giving tied values the average of their ranks. If the groups do not differ, each group’s ranks should be spread evenly through the pool. If one group’s values tend to be larger, its ranks will pile up at the top. U counts, over all possible pairs of one person from each group, how many times the group-1 person has the larger value.

blocks.label: Derivation
blocks.html:
1. Suppose every member of group 1 (size n₁) has a smaller value than everyone in group 2. Their ranks are 1, 2, … , n₁, with sum n₁(n₁ + 1)/2, and they exceed nobody: U₁ = 0.
  2. Each time a group-1 value moves above one group-2 value, that person’s rank rises by 1 and U₁ rises by 1.
  3. So U₁ = R₁ − n₁(n₁ + 1)/2, where R₁ is group 1’s rank sum. With n₁n₂ pairs in all, U₁ + U₂ = n₁n₂.
  4. Under H₀, U₁ has mean n₁n₂/2 and SD √[n₁n₂(N + 1)/12], where N = n₁ + n₂; for larger groups, z = (U₁ − n₁n₂/2) ÷ SD is referred to the Normal curve.

blocks.label: Illustration / Example
blocks.html: In the CBHI household survey (500 households, 150 members), is the distance from the health facility different for member and non-member households? Median distance is 6.9 km for members and 8.5 km for non-members.

blocks.label: Worked Calculation
blocks.html:
1. Rank all 500 distances. The members’ rank sum is R₁ = 29,758.5 (mean rank 198.4; non-members’ mean rank 272.8).
  2. U₁ = 29,758.5 − 150 × 151/2 = 29,758.5 − 11,325 = 18,433.5. U₀ = 150 × 350 − 18,433.5 = 34,066.5.
  3. U₁ ÷ (n₁n₀) = 18,433.5 ÷ 52,500 = 0.35. Pick one member and one non-member at random: the member lives farther away only about 35% of the time (ties counted as half). Under H₀ this would be 50%.
  4. Under H₀, mean U = 26,250 and SD = √(52,500 × 501/12) = 1,480.5. z = (18,433.5 − 26,250) ÷ 1,480.5 = −5.28, p ≈ 1 × 10⁻⁷.

blocks.label: In R (optional)
blocks.html:
cb <- read.csv("data/cbhi_survey.csv")
tapply(cb$distance_km, cb$cbhi_member, median)  # 0 = no, 1 = member
wilcox.test(distance_km ~ cbhi_member, data = cb)
  0   1 
8.5 6.9 

    Wilcoxon rank sum test with continuity correction

data:  distance_km by cbhi_member
W = 34066, p-value = 1.293e-07
alternative hypothesis: true location shift is not equal to 0

R’s W is U for the first group listed (non-members), 34,066.5 from step 2, printed rounded. The p-value (1.3 × 10⁻⁷) matches step 4 after R’s small corrections for ties and continuity.

points.html: Assumptions: observations independent within and between groups; an outcome that can at least be ordered.

It is a test of medians only when the two distributions have the same shape and differ just by a shift. When shapes or spreads differ, it can be significant even with similar medians (Hart, 2001). Here the member distances are more spread out (IQR 3.5–9.2 km) than the non-member distances (6.6–10.2 km), so report the result as “members tend to live closer”, with the medians as a description, not as “the medians differ”.
